title: Foreign investors sell W20.3tr in Korean stocks, led by SK hynix and Samsung Electronics
key_facts: Foreign investors sold a net 20.3 trillion won ($15.1 billion) of Kospi shares from 1 Sep to 2 Oct 2026 (Korea Exchange and Yonhap Infomax data, reported Sunday 4 Oct)
SK hynix (net 12.0 trillion won) and Samsung Electronics (5.2 trillion won) made up most of the selling
Foreign ownership of SK hynix fell to 49.76 percent, lowest since May 2023; foreign share of total Kospi value fell to 39.66 percent
Analysts cite profit-taking after big chip gains, the prolonged US-Iran conflict and rising interest rates
Selling eased at the start of October: net buying of 243 billion won on 1 Oct, selling of 190 billion won on 2 Oct
Micron beat expectations on 30 Sep; Samsung preliminary Q3 results expected around 8 Oct
quote_evidence: Foreign investors sold a net 20.3 trillion won ($15.1 billion) worth of shares on South Korea's main Kospi market over the past month, with semiconductor heavyweights SK hynix and Samsung Electronics accounting for most of the outflow, market data showed Sunday.
Foreign ownership of SK hynix stood at 49.76 percent as of Oct. 2, its lowest level since May 2023.
why_it_matters_hint: Foreign money is pulling back from the two memory-chip makers that supply the AI build
event_date: 1 Sep to 2 Oct 2026 data, reported 4 Oct 2026
notes: Korea Herald own reporting on exchange data.
